knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"

```{r setup, include = FALSE}
library(mighty.metadata)
```

This vignette walks you through the key workflows for defining and working with
ADaM specifications: loading and editing a single domain, assembling a
multi-domain study, propagating metadata across domains, applying conditional
includes and row subsets, managing documents and codelists, and producing flat
output for downstream tooling.

mighty.metadata manages *specifications* (metadata) only; it does not read or
create ADaM datasets.

All examples use the specifications bundled with the package in
`system.file("examples", package = "mighty.metadata")`, so every code chunk can
be run as-is. One chunk also uses the withr package, which can be installed
with `install.packages("withr")`.

To start your own study, copy the bundled examples to a new directory and edit
the YAML files there:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
dir.create("specs")
file.copy(
  list.files(
    system.file("examples", package = "mighty.metadata"),
    full.names = TRUE
  ),
  "specs"
)
study <- mighty_study("specs")
```

## The YAML Specification Format

Each ADaM domain is defined in a YAML file. The simplest case is a
subject-level dataset like ADSL, which has no parameters or rows:

```yaml
id: ADSL
label: Subject-Level Analysis Dataset
class: SUBJECT LEVEL ANALYSIS DATASET
structure: One record per subject
keys: USUBJID

population:
  base:
    - domain: DM
      depends: USUBJID
      filter: USUBJID != ""
  global:
    - filter: RANDFL == "Y"
      depends: RANDFL

columns:
  - id: STUDYID
    label: Study Identifier
    method: DM.STUDYID
    core: Req
  - id: USUBJID
    label: Unique Subject Identifier
    method: DM.USUBJID
    core: Req
  # ... more columns ...
```

A domain file is made up of three parts, described in turn below:
domain-level fields (`id`, `label`, `class`, `structure`, `keys`), the
optional `population` block, and the `columns` list.

### Domain-level fields

| Field        | Required | Description |
|--------------|----------|-------------|
| `id`         | yes      | Dataset name, uppercase (e.g. `ADSL`) |
| `label`      | yes      | Dataset label |
| `class`      | yes      | `SUBJECT LEVEL ANALYSIS DATASET`, `BASIC DATA STRUCTURE`, `OCCURRENCE DATA STRUCTURE` or `ADAM OTHER` |
| `structure`  | yes      | Description of one record |
| `keys`       | yes      | One key or a list of unique keys |
| `columns`    | yes      | List of columns |
| `subclass`   | no       | E.g. `TIME-TO-EVENT`, `ADVERSE EVENT` |
| `population` | no       | Source domains and filters used by the mighty code generator |
| `parameters` | no       | BDS parameters |
| `rows`       | no       | Row-level actions |
| `usecore`    | no       | Receive ADSL core variables (see `populate_core()`) |
| `include`    | no       | Conditional inclusion (see [Conditional Metadata]) |
| `comment`, `documents` | no | Free-text comment and document references |

All `id`s (domains, columns, parameters, rows) must be uppercase and match
`^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]*$`. Unknown fields are not allowed in domains, columns,
parameters, rows or `population` entries.

### Population

The optional `population` block declares which source domains supply raw data
and how the starting population is restricted. If present, it must contain
`base`; `global` is optional:

| Field    | Required fields per entry       | Description |
|----------|---------------------------------|-------------|
| `base`   | `domain`, `depends`, `filter`   | Source domains, each with its own filter |
| `global` | `filter`, `depends`             | Filters applied after combining the base datasets |

In the ADSL example above, records are taken from `DM` (where `USUBJID` is not
empty) and then restricted to randomized subjects (`RANDFL == "Y"`). The mighty
code generator reads this block to build the initial population step;
mighty.metadata stores it but does not execute it.

### Column fields

Only `id` is required. The most common fields are:

| Field       | Description |
|-------------|-------------|
| `label`     | Column label |
| `method`    | How the column is derived. `DOMAIN.COLUMN` (e.g. `DM.STUDYID`) marks a predecessor |
| `origin`    | `Assigned`, `Collected`, `Derived`, `Not Available`, `Other`, `Predecessor` or `Protocol` |
| `core`      | ADaM conformance: `Req`, `Cond` or `Perm` |
| `codelist`  | Id of a codelist in `_codelists.yml` |
| `format`    | `type` and `length` (both required) and optional SAS `display` format |
| `is_core`   | In ADSL: propagate the column to other domains |
| `depends`   | Dependencies: `COLUMN`, `DOMAIN.COLUMN`, `rows.ID` or `parameters.ID` |
| `component` | mighty component (`id` and optional `with` arguments) used for the derivation |
| `include`, `comment`, `documents` | Conditional inclusion, comment and document references |

A predecessor column (`method: DM.STUDYID`) can inherit its metadata from the
referenced column via `populate_sparse()`, provided the referenced domain is
part of the study.

For example, a fully specified derived column:

```yaml
- id: AGE
  label: Age
  origin: Derived
  core: Req
  method: Age at informed consent
  format:
    type: integer
    length: 3
  depends: [DM.BRTHDTC, DM.RFICDTC]
```

### BDS domains

A domain can also have `parameters` and `rows`; they are typically used in BDS
domains like ADVS. A parameter overrides column metadata in `columns` for its
records (e.g. `AVAL` for `BMI`); a row describes an action that adds or
modifies records (e.g. baseline, LOCF):

```yaml
id: ADVS
label: Vital Signs Analysis Dataset
class: BASIC DATA STRUCTURE
structure: One record per vital sign parameter, per visit, per subject
keys: [USUBJID, PARAMCD, AVISITN]

columns:
  # ... columns ...

parameters:
  - id: BMI
    label: Body Mass Index (kg/m^2)
    columns:
      - id: AVAL
        method: Derived from height and weight

rows:
  - id: BASELINE
    method: Add baseline visit as a new row
```

Parameters require only `id` and may also have `label`, `columns`,
`component`, `depends` and `include`. Rows require only `id` and may also have
`method`, `component`, `depends`, `subset` and `include`.

See `vignette("adam-schema")` for the full schema reference.

## Working with a Single Domain

The package provides a consistent set of verbs for columns, parameters, and
rows:

| Action | Columns              | Parameters              | Rows              |
|--------|----------------------|-------------------------|--------------------|
| List   | `list_columns()`     | `list_parameters()`     | `list_rows()`      |
| Select | `select_column()`    | `select_parameter()`    | `select_row()`     |
| Add    | `add_column()`       | `add_parameter()`       | `add_row()`        |
| Update | `update_column()`    | `update_parameter()`    | `update_row()`     |
| Move   | `move_column()`      | `move_parameter()`      | `move_row()`       |
| Remove | `remove_columns()`   | `remove_parameters()`   | `remove_rows()`    |

The `remove_*` functions accept a character vector to remove multiple items at
once.

### Loading and Inspecting

Load a domain specification from a YAML file with `mighty_domain()`. The file is
validated against the ADaM JSON schema on load.

```{r}
path <- system.file("examples", "advs.yml", package = "mighty.metadata")
advs <- mighty_domain(path)
advs
```

A domain can also be created from a list in memory with `.data`, e.g. when
specifications are generated programmatically:

```{r}
mighty_domain(
  .data = list(
    id = "ADXX",
    label = "Example Dataset",
    class = "ADAM OTHER",
    structure = "One record per subject",
    keys = "USUBJID",
    columns = list(list(id = "USUBJID", label = "Unique Subject Identifier"))
  )
)
```

A `mighty_domain` is a list, so any field can be read with `$` or `[[`:

```{r}
advs$keys
```

Use `list_*()` functions to see what the specification contains:

```{r}
list_columns(advs)
list_parameters(advs)
list_rows(advs)
```

Drill into a specific column with `select_column()`:

```{r}
select_column(advs, id = "AVAL") |>
  str()
```

### Modifying Columns

Every modification automatically re-validates the domain against the schema.
All column functions return the modified domain, so they compose naturally into
a pipe chain. Here we add an actual treatment column sourced from ADSL, update
a label, and drop an unused column:

```{r}
advs <- mighty_domain(path) |>
  add_column(
    id = "TRTA",
    label = "Actual Treatment",
    method = "ADSL.TRT01A",
    .pos = 5
  ) |>
  update_column(id = "AVAL", label = "Analysis Value (Numeric)") |>
  move_column(id = "PARAM", .pos = 3) |>
  remove_columns(id = "AVALC")

list_columns(advs)
```

Any column field from the table above can be passed to `add_column()` and
`update_column()` as a named argument. `.pos` sets the position; by default
new items are appended at the end. `update_column()` only changes the given
fields and keeps the column's position.

#### Schema Validation

Validation runs on every modification and on initial load. You can also call
`validate()` explicitly at any time:

```{r}
validate(advs)
```

If a modification violates the schema, you get an immediate error. For example,
adding a column with a duplicate ID fails:

```{r, error = TRUE}
advs |> add_column(id = "AVAL", label = "Duplicate")
```

Values outside the controlled terminology are rejected as well:

```{r, error = TRUE}
advs |> update_column(id = "AVAL", origin = "Calculated")
```

### Modifying Parameters

Parameters use the same verbs. The key difference is the `columns` argument in
`add_parameter()`, which accepts a nested list of column overrides specific to
that parameter:

```{r}
select_parameter(advs, id = "BMI") |>
  str()
```

```{r}
advs <- advs |>
  add_parameter(
    id = "WSTCIR",
    label = "Waist Circumference (cm)",
    columns = list(
      list(id = "AVAL", method = "VS.VSSTRESN")
    )
  )

list_parameters(advs)
```

Update and remove work as expected:

```{r}
advs <- advs |>
  update_parameter(id = "WSTCIR", label = "Waist Circumference") |>
  remove_parameters(id = "BMIGRP")

list_parameters(advs)
```

### Rows

Rows follow the same pattern. Inspect a row with `select_row()`:

```{r}
select_row(advs, id = "BASELINE") |>
  str()
```

Add a row action that uses a mighty component, update it and change its
position:

```{r}
advs <- advs |>
  add_row(
    id = "LOCF",
    method = "Last observation carried forward",
    component = list(id = "locf", with = list(domain = "ADVS")),
    depends = "rows.BASELINE"
  ) |>
  update_row(id = "LOCF", method = "LOCF imputation for missing visits") |>
  move_row(id = "LOCF", .pos = 1)

list_rows(advs)
```

### Saving Changes

Write the modified domain back to YAML with `write_config()`:

```{r}
out <- tempfile(fileext = ".yml")
write_config(advs, path = out)
```

The written file can be loaded back with `mighty_domain()`.

## Working with a Study

### Loading a Study

Load all domain specifications from a directory with `mighty_study()`. Besides
the domain files, the directory can contain four optional study-level files:

| File              | Property     | Content                                   |
|-------------------|--------------|-------------------------------------------|
| `_study.yml`      | `@study`     | Study-level properties (`study_config()`) |
| `_mighty.yml`     | `@mighty`    | mighty framework configuration (`mighty_config()`) |
| `_documents.yml`  | `@documents` | Study documents (`mighty_documents()`)    |
| `_codelists.yml`  | `@codelists` | Study codelists (`mighty_codelists()`)    |

All other YAML files are loaded as domains and their file names must start with
`ad` or `md` (case-insensitive); any other name is an error.

```{r}
study_path <- system.file("examples", package = "mighty.metadata")
study <- mighty_study(study_path)
study
```

The bundled examples include all four study-level files. When a file is
absent, `mighty_study()` prints a message; `@documents` and `@codelists` are
then empty, while `@study` and `@mighty` are `NULL`.

Access individual domains with `$` and study-level properties with `@`:

```{r}
names(study)
study@study$study_id
study@mighty$repos
```

The `_study.yml` file provides the `study_id`, and optionally the `standards`
and `terminology` (controlled terminologies and dictionaries) applied in the
study. Each entry requires an `id` and a `version`:

```yaml
study_id: example_study

standards:
  - id: ADaM-IG
    version: '1.1'

terminology:
  - id: ADAM
    version: '2025-08-06'
  - id: MedDRA
    version: '22.1'
  - id: WHODrug
    version: 2023 JAN
```

`version` must be a string, so quote values that look like numbers or dates
(`'1.1'`, not `1.1`). Only the structure is validated; whether a version
exists is left to consuming packages. See `vignette("study-schema")`.

```{r}
study@study$standards |>
  purrr::map_chr("id")
```

The `_mighty.yml` file configures the mighty framework. Both fields are
required: `external_data` lists the source (e.g. SDTM) domains with their
keys, and `repos` lists the repositories where mighty components are found,
as local paths or `owner/repo/subdir@ref` strings:

```yaml
external_data:
  - id: DM
    keys: [STUDYID, USUBJID]
  - id: VS
    keys: [STUDYID, USUBJID]

repos:
  - "NovoNordisk-OpenSource/mighty.standards/components@main"
  - "."
```

See `vignette("mighty-schema")` for details.

Loading messages, such as the ones printed for missing study-level files, can
be silenced with the `mighty.metadata.verbosity_level` option (see
`?"mighty.metadata-options"`):

```{r}
withr::with_options(
  list(mighty.metadata.verbosity_level = "quiet"),
  mighty_study(study_path)
)
```

`filter_domains()` keeps only domains whose names start with given prefixes,
e.g. to drop `MD*` domains:

```{r}
study |>
  filter_domains(prefix = "AD") |>
  names()
```

### Populating Core Variables

A "core variable" is an ADSL column that should appear in every consumer domain
(ADVS, ADAE, etc.) as a predecessor column --- for example, SEX and RACE for
subgroup analyses.

Note: `core` (string: Req/Cond/Perm) records the ADaM conformance level and is
unrelated to "core variable" propagation. The two fields that control
propagation are:

- `is_core` (Boolean, column-level in ADSL) --- marks a column for propagation
  to consumer domains.
- `usecore` (Boolean, domain-level) --- signals that a domain should receive the
  propagated columns. This is a top-level YAML property on the consumer domain,
  so it is set via list assignment rather than `update_column()`.

`populate_core()` reads these flags and appends the marked ADSL columns to the
end of each consumer domain as predecessor columns (`method: ADSL.<COLUMN>`,
`origin: Predecessor`). It errors if a consumer domain already has a column
with the same name, and only ADSL may mark columns with `is_core`.

In YAML this looks like:

```yaml
# adsl.yml
columns:
  - id: SEX
    label: Sex
    is_core: true

# adae.yml
id: ADAE
usecore: true
```

The bundled examples do not include these fields, so we add them here to
demonstrate the workflow:

```{r}
study$ADSL <- study$ADSL |>
  update_column(id = "SEX", is_core = TRUE) |>
  update_column(id = "RACE", is_core = TRUE)

study$ADAE[["usecore"]] <- TRUE

study <- study |>
  populate_core()

list_columns(study$ADAE)
```

SEX and RACE now appear in ADAE as predecessor columns sourced from ADSL.

### Populating Predecessor Metadata

Columns that reference another domain (e.g., `method: ADSL.SAFFL`) can inherit
metadata from the referenced column. `populate_sparse()` performs this lookup
across the study for every predecessor column (`method: DOMAIN.COLUMN` or
`origin: Predecessor`):

- `origin` is set to `Predecessor`.
- Properties missing in the column (e.g. `label`, `format`, `codelist`) are
  copied from the referenced column; existing properties are not overwritten.
  `id`, `method`, `origin`, `is_core`, `component` and `depends` are never
  copied.
- If the referenced domain is not in the study (e.g. SDTM `DM`), only `origin`
  is set. If the domain exists but the column does not, it is an error.

```{r}
# Before: SAFFL in ADVS references ADSL.SAFFL
select_column(study$ADVS, id = "SAFFL") |>
  str()
```

```{r}
study <- study |> populate_sparse()

# After: origin set to Predecessor
select_column(study$ADVS, id = "SAFFL") |>
  str()
```

### The Complete Study Pipeline

Here is the full pipeline in one block:

```{r}
study <- mighty_study(study_path)

# Mark ADSL core variables
study$ADSL <- study$ADSL |>
  update_column(id = "SEX", is_core = TRUE) |>
  update_column(id = "RACE", is_core = TRUE)

# Mark consumer domains
study$ADAE[["usecore"]] <- TRUE

# Run the pipeline
study <- study |>
  populate_core() |>
  populate_sparse()
```

If your YAML files already include the `is_core` and `usecore` flags, the
entire pipeline collapses to a single call. Passing `populate = TRUE` is
equivalent to calling `populate_core()` then `populate_sparse()` after loading:

```{r}
study <- mighty_study(study_path, populate = TRUE)
```

### Saving a Study

Write all domain files back to disk with `write_config()`. `_study.yml` and
`_mighty.yml` are written when `@study` and `@mighty` are set, and
`_documents.yml` and `_codelists.yml` when `@documents` and `@codelists` are
not empty:

```{r}
out <- tempfile()
dir.create(out)
write_config(study, path = out)
list.files(out)
```

Omit `path` to write back to the original directory (`study@path`).

## Conditional Metadata

Pooled specifications can serve multiple studies by using conditional `include`
fields. Conditions are wrapped in `{braces}` and evaluated as R expressions
(via `glue::glue_data()`) against the study's `@study` values. `include` can
also be a plain `true` or `false`:

```yaml
columns:
  - id: STUDYID
    label: Study Identifier
    include: "{study_id == 'example_study'}"
  - id: SITEID
    label: Study Site Identifier
    include: false
```

The same condition set in R:

```{r}
study <- mighty_study(study_path)

study$ADVS <- study$ADVS |>
  update_column(
    id = "STUDYID",
    include = "{study_id == 'example_study'}"
  )
```

When `study_id` in `@study` matches, the condition is `TRUE` and the column is
kept:

```{r}
resolved <- resolve_includes(study)
list_columns(resolved$ADVS)
```

Override with a different value and the column is removed:

```{r}
resolved <- resolve_includes(study, info = list(study_id = "other"))
list_columns(resolved$ADVS)
```

`include` can be applied to whole domains, columns, rows, parameters, and
individual columns within a parameter. A domain whose condition is `FALSE` is
removed from the study. `info` can hold any values used in the conditions,
not only `study_id`.

### Row Subsets

A row action can be restricted to a subset of the source rows with the `subset`
field. The row must have a `component` with a `with.domain` entry.
`resolve_subsets()` folds the subset into `component.with.domain` as a
`.mighty_subset()` marker call, which `mighty.component` (>= 0.1.0.9003)
expands when rendering code:

```yaml
rows:
  - id: TRTEMFL_STUDY1
    subset: STUDYID == 'STUDY1'
    component:
      id: STUDY1_COMPONENT
      with:
        domain: ADAE
```

The same row added in R:

```{r}
study$ADAE <- study$ADAE |>
  add_row(
    id = "TRTEMFL_STUDY1",
    component = list(id = "STUDY1_COMPONENT", with = list(domain = "ADAE")),
    subset = "STUDYID == 'STUDY1'"
  )

study |>
  resolve_subsets() |>
  getElement("ADAE") |>
  select_row(id = "TRTEMFL_STUDY1") |>
  str()
```

## Documents

Study-level documents (e.g. the SAP) are stored in `_documents.yml` and
available as `@documents`. Each document has an `id`, `title`, `href` and a
`doctype` of `"suppdoc"`, `"comment"` or `"method"`. The bundled
`_documents.yml` contains:

```yaml
- id: SAP
  title: Statistical Analysis Plan
  doctype: suppdoc
  href: ./docs/sap.pdf

- id: DERIV_METHODS
  title: Derivation Methods
  doctype: method
  href: ./docs/methods.pdf
```

```{r}
list_documents(study)
```

Domains and columns (including columns within parameters) reference documents
by `id` in their `documents` field, optionally with a `page`:

```yaml
columns:
  - id: SAFFL
    label: Safety Population Flag
    origin: Derived
    documents:
      - id: DERIV_METHODS
        page: 12
```

The `list_documents()`, `select_document()`, `add_document()`,
`update_document()` and `remove_documents()` verbs work on both a study and a
`mighty_documents()` object:

```{r}
study <- study |>
  add_document(
    id = "PROTOCOL",
    title = "Study Protocol",
    doctype = "suppdoc",
    href = "./docs/protocol.pdf"
  )

list_documents(study)
```

References can also be added in R:

```{r}
study$ADSL <- study$ADSL |>
  update_column(id = "SAFFL", documents = list(list(id = "SAP", page = 12)))
```

`check_document_references()` verifies that every referenced document exists,
that `"method"` documents are only used where `origin` is `"Derived"`, and warns
when a `"comment"` document is referenced without a `comment`:

```{r}
check_document_references(study)
```

## Codelists

Codelists are stored in `_codelists.yml` and available as `@codelists`. A
codelist is either sponsor-defined (`values`) or records changes to an external
codelist, such as CDISC CT, through `subset`, `restore` and `extend`. The
bundled `_codelists.yml` contains one sponsor-defined codelist (`SEX`) and one
that modifies an external codelist (`AGEU`, via `subset` and `restore`):

```yaml
# Sponsor-defined codelist
- id: SEX
  label: Sex
  description: Sex of the subject
  datatype: text
  values:
    - code: F
      decode: Female
    - code: M
      decode: Male

# Keep only some values of an external codelist and restore one more
- id: AGEU
  subset:
    - code: YEARS
  restore:
    - code: MONTHS
```

```{r}
list_codelists(study)
select_codelist(study, id = "SEX") |>
  str()
```

Columns refer to a codelist by its `id` in their `codelist` field, as `SEX`
and `AGEU` do in the bundled `adsl.yml`:

```yaml
columns:
  - id: SEX
    label: Sex
    codelist: SEX
```

Codelists can also be added in R. Here we add a sponsor-defined value to the
extensible external `LOC` codelist:

```{r}
study <- study |>
  extend_codelist_values(
    id = "LOC",
    code = "MY CUSTOM LOCATION",
    decode = "My Custom Location"
  )

list_codelists(study)
```

Codelists can be added before any column uses them. Use
`check_codelist_references()` to check that every codelist is referenced:

```{r, error = TRUE}
check_codelist_references(study)
```

```{r}
study$ADVS <- study$ADVS |>
  add_column(
    id = "VSLOC",
    label = "Location of Vital Signs Measurement",
    codelist = "LOC"
  )

check_codelist_references(study)
```

See `vignette("codelists-schema")` for all operation groups and validation
rules, and `?list_codelists` for all codelist verbs.

## Creating Flat Metadata Tables

A set of `create_md_*()` functions flattens the study specifications into
tibbles. This is the format consumed by downstream mighty tools.

`create_md_table()` gives one row per dataset:

```{r}
create_md_table(study)
```

`create_md_col()` gives one row per column:

```{r}
create_md_col(study)
```

`create_md_param()` gives one row per BDS parameter:

```{r}
create_md_param(study)
```

`create_md_values()` gives one row per column defined inside a parameter,
i.e. the value level metadata:

```{r}
create_md_values(study)
```

The tables reflect the study as it is, so populate and resolve it first.
A typical end-to-end workflow:

```{r}
md_col <- mighty_study(study_path, populate = TRUE) |>
  resolve_includes() |>
  resolve_subsets() |>
  create_md_col()

md_col
```

## Next Steps

This vignette covered the core workflows: `mighty_domain()` for single datasets,
`mighty_study()` for collections, `populate_core()` and `populate_sparse()` for
metadata propagation, `write_config()` for saving changes, `resolve_includes()`
and `resolve_subsets()` for conditional specifications, documents and
codelists, and the `create_md_*()` functions for flat output.

To learn more:

- `vignette("adam-schema")` documents the domain YAML schema reference
- `vignette("study-schema")` documents the study YAML schema reference
- `vignette("mighty-schema")` documents the mighty YAML schema reference
- `vignette("codelists-schema")` documents the codelists YAML schema reference
- The [package reference](https://novonordisk-opensource.github.io/mighty.metadata/reference/index.html)
  lists all available functions
